key_insight: GraphBEAT outperformed tested graph and sequence models for early gastrointestinal cancer risk prediction while using substantially less computation.
clinical_relevance: This research could support earlier risk stratification for pancreatic, liver, and intestinal cancers; it addresses risk prediction, not cancer drug discovery.
method: Groups diagnosis codes and laboratory results into time buckets and patient-specific temporal graphs.
Encodes event identity, observed value, and timing, with context-aware, time-decay message passing.
Uses multi-head attention pooling to generate patient-level representations.
evidence_signal: In multi-site longitudinal EHR evaluations at 12-, 24-, and 36-month diagnostic lead times, GraphBEAT outperformed all tested baselines and required over 250× fewer FLOPs per patient and over 20× fewer parameters than Transformer and LSTM baselines.
watch_item: The abstract does not report absolute predictive performance or prospective clinical validation, leaving real-world utility uncertain.
paper_title: GraphBEAT: Graph-based Bucketized Event Aggregation Over Time for Early Risk Stratification of Gastrointestinal Cancers
